title: Combatting the ghost of Demoralization
summary: NH argues that demoralization, a complete loss of hope in one's own agency, is the most important and least discussed mental obstacle to progress, worse than depression or anxiety. He blames external sources including the supplement-driven fitness industry, and prescribes relentless action and years of consistent training as the only way out.
claims: A depressed or anxious person can still make gains, but a demoralized person will never progress
Mental state affects physical state: if you don't believe in yourself your body will never grow
Most people who blame genetics and think they can't grow are highly demoralized
Demoralization is a complete lack of hope: believing your actions have no impact and you're at the mercy of outside forces and luck
Demoralization is inflicted by others telling you what you can't do, and most seemingly positive messages are manipulation to sell you something
Only you can pull yourself out of low morale
Most Cold War budgets went to demoralization and propaganda rather than spying or attacks
YouTube fitness is a factory of demoralization: it shames you about what you lack so you buy supplements that don't work
The solution is not meditation, prayer or reading but action: train day in and day out regardless of doubts
Many people give up because they think they aren't progressing, creating a self-fulfilling prophecy
For a skinny young man transformation takes years, not weeks or months
He was highly demoralized as a teen and lifting saved him; growing up mostly offline let him build resilience
Disconnect from negative inputs, including YouTube and his own channel if it doesn't help, and focus on yourself
Demoralization comes from outside sources, not the self; school never taught you to filter negative influences
Feeling at 17-18 that your life is over is a lie; the only way out of the fog is to keep walking
